Let me analyze this specification. It's about Hyperledger Fabric v1.0 development. The user stories are:

U1: New visitor getting started - documentation/onboarding improvements
U2: Document new-channel configuration transaction (fields, values) - documentation of channel config transaction structure
U3: Peer upgrade capability without data loss - protocol upgrade support
U4: Fix ledger code/tests using old block structure, remove MSP dependency from ledger unit tests
U5: Explain/show architecture with visual aids and scripts - demos/documentation
U6: Up-to-date documentation for v1.0, directing to v0.6 for stable - documentation
U7: Sanity check on chaincode invocation (only LSCC/LCCC or normal chaincode) - code change in chaincode invocation validation
U8: Node SDK for NodeJS application development

Wait, "LCCC" here — in Fabric v1.0 it's LSCC (Lifecycle System Chaincode). The story says "LCCC" (probably "Lifecycle Chain Code" early naming). I'll treat it as LSCC.

I need to break this into WBS activities, provide most likely effort estimates in workdays, and sum.

2. U1: Getting-started / onboarding documentation improvements
3. U2: New-channel configuration transaction documentation (fields, values, examples)
4. U3: Peer upgrade mechanism design and implementation (protocol upgrade without data loss)
5. U4: Ledger code refactor to new block structure + test updates + remove MSP dependency
6. U5: Architecture presentation materials, visual aids, demo scripts
7. U6: v1.0 developer documentation + v0.6 redirection notices
8. U7: Chaincode invocation sanity check (restrict invocation to LSCC or normal chaincodes)
9. U8: Node SDK development
10. Integration testing, CI, code review, release

Let me estimate each in workdays (single developer, most likely):

U3 is a big one: peer upgrade with protocol change, no data loss. Design + implementation + migration tooling + tests. Maybe 20-25 days.

U8 Node SDK is big: a Node.js SDK for Fabric — enrollment, transaction submission, channels, etc. Could be 30-40 days for an initial version. Let me say 35.

U4: ledger refactor to new block structure + test fixes + decouple MSP. Maybe 8-10 days.

U7: sanity check in chaincode shim/peer — small, 2-3 days.

U1: getting started docs/quickstart — 4-5 days.

U2: channel config transaction doc — 3-4 days.

U5: presentation, visual aids, demo scripts — 5 days.

U6: v1.0 docs restructure + v0.6 redirect — 6-8 days.

Plus integration/system testing, code review, CI: 8-10 days.

106 workdays total. That seems plausible for this increment.

Maybe I could keep it a bit leaner. Let me reconsider. Some might argue the Node SDK alone is huge (in reality it was a multi-person effort over months). For a single developer doing initial functional SDK: 30+ days. Fine.

Peer upgrade U3: in reality Fabric v1.0 had "upgrade" via docker images and data compatibility; designing upgrade path could be ~15-20 days total. Fine.

Let me finalize with maybe 14-16 activities. Ensure all effort numbers > 0.

- Target Hyperledger Fabric v1.0 architecture (peers, orderers, channels, chaincode, MSP).

technical_and_design_decisions: Target the Hyperledger Fabric v1.0 architecture (peers, ordering service, channels, chaincode, MSP) as the codebase baseline for all implementation work.

For U3, use the lifecycle system chaincode (LSCC, referred to as LCCC in the story) for chaincode-level upgrades and a system-chaincode-based patching path for non-protocol fixes; protocol upgrades are handled via a versioned peer binary plus a data-format compatibility/migration layer so existing ledger data is preserved.

For U4, migrate all remaining ledger code and ledger tests to the new block structure (common.Block with BlockHeader/BlockData/Envelope payloads) introduced by Gerrit change 2581, and refactor ledger unit tests to use lightweight mock security primitives instead of the real MSP implementation.

For U7, enforce the invocation sanity check in the peer's chaincode support/endorser path: only normal (application) chaincodes or the lifecycle system chaincode may be invoked; any other system chaincode invocation is rejected.

For U2, document the new-channel configuration transaction as a common.Envelope carrying a ConfigEnvelope (channel group hierarchy, mod_policy, values such as Consortium/ChannelCreationPolicy/AnchorPeers, and signatures), aligned with the API from FAB-687 and Gerrit change 1795.

For U8, build the Node SDK in Node.js (JavaScript) using gRPC with protobuf stubs generated from the Fabric protocol definitions; the SDK wraps fabric-ca for enrollment and exposes client/channel/peer/transaction-proposal/query/event APIs.

All documentation (U1, U2, U5, U6) is authored in reStructuredText/Markdown and published through the project's documentation pipeline (ReadTheDocs), with v0.6 content clearly separated and redirected from v1.0 pages.
Unit tests accompany each code activity; integration/system verification and code review are captured as separate cross-cutting activities.
assumptions: A single developer (myself) performs all work; all figures are effort in workdays (1 workday = 8 hours), not elapsed calendar time.
A working Fabric v1.0 development/build environment (Go toolchain, Docker, Gerrit access) and the referenced changes 1795 and 2581 are available.

Node SDK scope (U8) is an initial functional release covering identity enrollment, channel create/join interaction, chaincode install/instantiate/invoke/query, and event listening; full production hardening and advanced features are out of scope for this increment.

U3 covers design plus a reference implementation and test evidence of a protocol-upgrade path with data preservation for the current v1.0 codebase, not a generalized solution for all possible future protocol changes.
U5 deliverables are presentation slides, architecture diagrams/visual aids, and runnable demo scripts describing v1.0 as of approximately sprint 6.
U6 documentation covers the in-development v1.0 usage docs plus clear redirection of users seeking a stable platform to v0.6 docs.
Documentation is produced in English only; no localization effort is included.
Existing continuous integration infrastructure is in place, so only increment-specific CI/test-job adjustments are included.

activities.activity_description: Analyze all user stories against the current v1.0 codebase, review referenced Gerrit changes (1795, 2581) and FAB-687, define the overall technical approach, and produce short design notes for the upgrade path, invocation sanity check, and Node SDK scope.

Create and restructure quick-start and navigation content so new visitors can get started quickly and find what they need: landing page, prerequisites, install/run first network, and pointers to key topics.

Document the new-channel configuration transaction produced by the FAB-687 API: structure (Envelope/ConfigEnvelope), all fields, allowed values, policies, and worked examples; reconcile with Gerrit change 1795.

Design the peer upgrade mechanism for protocol changes without data loss: versioning of data formats, compatibility/migration approach, interaction with LSCC-based chaincode upgrades and SCC-based patching, and rollback considerations.

Implement the upgrade support: data-format version markers, ledger/state migration logic executed on peer startup after a protocol change, SCC patch-application path for non-protocol fixes, and operational documentation for performing the upgrade.

Write and run tests proving upgrade with no data loss: pre-upgrade data creation, upgrade execution, post-upgrade validation of ledger/world state and chaincode operation, plus negative/rollback scenarios.

activities.activity_name: U4: Migrate remaining ledger code to new block structure
activities.activity_description: Fix the remaining portions of ledger code that still use the old block structure missed by Gerrit change 2581, including transaction construction previously embedded inside ledger tests.

activities.activity_name: U4: Refactor ledger tests and remove MSP dependency
activities.activity_description: Update ledger unit tests to the new block structure and remove their explicit dependency on MSP/security components by introducing mock or stub security primitives.

activities.activity_name: U5: Architecture presentation, visual aids and demo scripts
activities.activity_description: Produce slides and architecture diagrams of Fabric v1.0 (as of ~sprint 6) plus runnable demonstration scripts that show current behavior to collaborators and potential customers.

activities.activity_name: U6: v1.0 developer documentation and v0.6 redirection
activities.activity_description: Maintain up-to-date v1.0 usage documentation reflecting ongoing development, and add clear redirection/labeling so users seeking a stable operational platform are directed to v0.6 documentation.

Implement validation in the peer chaincode-support/endorser path so that only normal chaincodes or the lifecycle system chaincode can be invoked; add unit and integration tests for allowed and rejected invocations.

Design the Node.js SDK API surface: client, channel, peer/orderer handles, enrollment via fabric-ca, transaction proposal flow, query, and event subscription; define module structure and generated gRPC/protobuf stubs.

Implement the SDK: identity enrollment and key storage, channel create/join support, chaincode install/instantiate/invoke/query flows, endorsement proposal assembly and signing, and event hub/event listener integration.

activities.activity_name: U8: Node SDK tests and sample application
activities.activity_description: Write unit and integration tests for the SDK against a running v1.0 network, and deliver a sample Node.js application demonstrating end-to-end usage (enroll, deploy chaincode, invoke, query, receive events).

activities.activity_name: Cross-cutting integration, review and defect fixing
activities.activity_description: Integrate all work items, run full regression and CI pipelines, address code review feedback via Gerrit, fix defects discovered during system testing, and prepare the increment for delivery.
